scope: explain the visible flicker reported by the user

measured.conclusion: the client state machine does NOT flip; the flicker is a render-layer symptom, not a state oscillation
measured.screenshot: runs/flicker-shot.png shows a pure black screen with the loading spinner in the bottom-right corner

server_side_during_flicker.client_inband: seq advancing, serverId 0, messageAck 1, 206 bytes, body all zero

interpretation.what_the_flicker_is: the loading screen redrawing repeatedly while waiting for a gamestate that never arrives
interpretation.why_the_client_waits: the 4-byte seq-only packets we send are not a valid netchan message; the client keeps its loader alive and keeps sending empty ack heartbeats
interpretation.why_it_matters: this is the first visually observable reaction from the client to our own server - it left the lobby and entered a loading state, but cannot finish because we have not sent a real gamestate

next: send a properly framed packet: seq(4) + serverId(1) + messageAck(4) + body, at least matching the 206-byte shape the client itself uses
then attempt a gamestate body so the loader can complete
keep the 200 ms state sampling running during the attempt so any transition is captured
